cars.variant: Series 1 XJ12, 9:1 carburetted V12 automatic — September 1972 English factory reference
cars.specification_market: Original Series 1 XJ12, 1972 English-language Jaguar factory brochure reference, 9:1 carburetted specification. Actual PDF index 9 specification page, print footer 9/72, supplies 5343 cc sixty-degree V12, one overhead camshaft per bank, four carburetters, 309 bhp gross at 6250 rpm and 332 lb-ft gross at 4000 rpm. Gross ratings are explicit and remain gross; no modern net output, inferred kW/Nm conversion, later fuel injection or HE calibration is substituted. Borg-Warner automatic with torque converter is specified; an unprinted model number or gear count is not inferred. The brochure warns that specifications vary by country, so this is its printed reference rather than a claim that every 1972 export car had this tune. Later long-wheelbase/Series 2/Series 3, Daimler trim, E-type V12 and Broadspeed race-car fields are not copied.
cars.summary: The XJ12 brought Jaguar’s 5.3-litre V12 into the classic XJ sports saloon, combining a twelve-cylinder performance engine with independent suspension and four-wheel disc brakes. It is a landmark of Jaguar’s fast, refined four-door tradition. Count the classic Series 1/2/3 XJ sporting-road family once across XJ6/XJ12, Daimler Sovereign/Double Six, bodies, wheelbases and years; no trim or later engine tune adds an extra entry.

cars.variant: X300 XJR AJ16 supercharged, optional GM four-speed automatic — 1995 European technical-guide reference
cars.specification_market: 1995 model-year X300 XJR 4.0 supercharged catalyst engine, selected European optional GM 4L80E four-speed automatic. Actual Jaguar August 1994 technical introduction JJM 10 15 12/50 supplies model/market availability and selected engine/transmission details. The 4.0 SC column gives 3980 cc, DOHC inline six/four valves per cylinder, 91 × 102 mm, 8.5:1, 240 kW DIN at 5000 rpm and 512 Nm DIN at 3050 rpm. The same table prints 326 PS and 321.8 BHP, which are different units; native kW/Nm are retained without recomputing or calling 326 mechanical bhp. Eaton M90 with belt drive and an air-to-liquid intake-manifold intercooler are explicit. The guide says the Getrag five-speed is standard in Europe and the selected GM automatic optional there; it is not labelled universally standard. The 2013 retrospective’s different power-unit wording is not technical authority. Normally aspirated 3.2/4.0, X300 6.0 V12, later X308 V8, pre-production Thrust fire-car modifications and XJR-15 race data are excluded.
cars.summary: The X300 XJR introduced supercharging to Jaguar’s R saloons. Its AJ16 straight-six paired an Eaton blower and liquid-cooled charge-air system with a production four-door body, establishing a defining strand of later Jaguar performance cars. Count this absent XJ40-derived X300/X308 sporting-saloon lineage once for now; naturally aspirated Sport trim, six-/eight-/twelve-cylinder variants, Daimler badges, transmissions and subsequent years do not add separate counts.
